name: Why CoDesign and when to engage
obj: Explain in two sentences what CoDesign is for and recognise the moments to bring the team in.
who: Everyone who meets clients: sales, account teams, BRMs (Business Relationship Managers), site and tech leads.
when: Before any client conversation about experience, renewal or a new site.
inputs: Account situation: contract end date, satisfaction trend, planned site changes.
steps: Spot a trigger: contract ends in 18 months or less, a priority client must be retained, satisfaction is slipping, a new site or refurbishment is planned
Check sponsorship: a senior client sponsor, an account owner and a tech owner
Call the CoDesign team for a Presales conversation (02)
quality: Engage early: 18 months before renewal works better than 2-3 months.
mistakes: Calling CoDesign for a one-off workshop at the last minute · no sponsor.
example: WORK: Northbridge restaurant contract renews in 16 months and attendance is flat → trigger met; sponsor = Head of Workplace. [fictional]

var.HEAL: Patient-experience scores falling two quarters in a row.

cred: Use named projects only; commercial figures need Arnaud's sign-off (see conflicts register).
prompt: Generic Claude prompt: 'Here is an account summary [paste]. Which CoDesign engagement triggers apply, and what 3 questions should I ask the client sponsor?'
l_obj: Identify an engagement trigger in an account description and name the sponsor needed.
explain: Clients don't renew a contract; they renew the experience they helped create. CoDesign brings users, frontline teams and sponsors into decisions early.

exercise.situation: Three account descriptions (one per segment pack).
questions: Is it too late, too early or right?

answer_key.sample_answer: Northbridge: 16 months, trigger met. Riverside: new stand, right time. St Aldric: falling scores, sponsor = director of patient experience.

name: Team, roles and regional operating model
obj: Know who does what in an engagement and where regional colleagues contribute.
who: CoDesign core team (method, facilitation, templates) · regional champions and local designers (local cases, supported delivery) · account, sales and BRMs (access, sponsorship, continuity) · tech pre-sales (capability fit).
acc: Proposed ownership (to confirm): Diane integration · Noël method and quality · Gabriel templates, evidence, OS mapping · Arnaud positioning and sponsor review.
steps: Find your role in the RACI
Check the capability level your role needs (N0-N4)
Agree supported tasks with the CoDesign lead
output: Your role and level for the engagement.
std: Every task has one accountable person.
quality: People act at the level they have shown, with coaching above it.
mistakes: Assuming attendance at training = independent delivery.
example: HEAL: on St Aldric the BRM Healthcare joins site visits as Contributor (N1) and co-facilitates one group (N2, coached). [fictional]

var.WORK: BRM Corporate co-hosts the Northbridge kick-off.

prompt: Planning & RACI agent with project scope and team list.
l_obj: Place yourself in a RACI and state your target level.
explain: The method scales through documentation, tooling and people close to the business.

exercise.situation: RACI for a Format A workshop project.

answer_key.sample_answer: Depends on role; sign-off sits with CoDesign lead and client sponsor.

name: End-to-end approach and the six-section campus
obj: Describe the end-to-end process: Presales, then the four Double Diamond phases.
steps: 02 Presales: frame the opportunity, before the Double Diamond
03 Discover: diverge on the problem with evidence
04 Define: converge on who, what hurts, where to act
05 Co-create: diverge on solutions with users and client
06 Test & Deliver: converge on tested, owned decisions
std: Learner can place any activity in the right section.
quality: Six campus sections = one introduction + five process sections. Presales precedes the four Double Diamond phases.
mistakes: Treating a half-day workshop as the whole engagement · skipping Discover.
handoff: → choose learning route (Format A or B).
example: WORK: Northbridge runs 02 → 06 over about 12 weeks; the half-day workshop is one day inside 05. [fictional]

var.PLAY: Riverside fits around the fixture calendar.
var.HEAL: St Aldric adds clinical review gates.

prompt: Generic Claude prompt: 'Sort these activities into the six campus sections and explain each placement in one line.'
verify: Placement against the six-section taxonomy on Start Here.
fallback: Card sort on the Start Here process strip.
l_obj: Sort 10 activity cards into the six sections.
explain: Diverge to explore, converge to decide — twice: first on the problem, then on the solution.

answer_key.sample_answer: Proposal 02; site visit 03; journey 04; idea sheet 05; value proposition 06; test 06.X3.

name: Human-led, AI-supported: how we use CoDesign OS
obj: Use AI support safely: the method works without AI; when used, a designer verifies, edits and decides.
steps: Do the step manually first in training
Use the OS agent with real context
Decide what stays — a human decision
output: AI output that is verified and owned by a person.
std: No unverified fact leaves the team.
quality: Readable without AI; prompts at the bottom of every card; human decides.
mistakes: Pasting confidential data into unapproved tools · treating AI ideas as evidence.
example: PLAY: Journey Map agent drafts Dev's matchday journey; the designer deletes two invented quotes and keeps the stage names.

var.WORK: Client Intelligence draft checked against the annual report.

tools: CoDesign OS (23 live agents, read 3 Nov 2026)
fallback: Every block has a manual fallback.
l_obj: Explain the three human checks applied to any AI output.
explain: Human first. AI second. Human decides.

exercise.situation: An AI-generated journey with 2 invented quotes.

answer_key.sample_answer: Quotes without transcript IDs; delete or tag [TO VALIDATE]; humans decide which opportunities go forward.
